title: Caring for the Umbilical Cord Stump
hook: The cord stump needs almost nothing — just keep it clean and dry and let it fall off on its own, usually within about three weeks. A few signs, though, mean call the doctor.
key_points: Keep the stump clean and dry; there's no need for alcohol or special products.
Stick to sponge baths until the stump falls off on its own — usually by about three weeks.
A little dried blood or spotting as it separates is normal; folding the diaper below it keeps it dry.
Call the doctor for redness around the base, foul-smelling discharge, pain when touched, active bleeding, or fever.
content_html: The umbilical cord stump looks like it should be high-maintenance, but it really isn't. The main job is to keep it clean and dry and let it shrivel and drop off on its own — usually by the time your baby is about three weeks old. The AAP notes there's no need for rubbing alcohol or special products; folding the diaper down below the stump helps keep it dry and exposed to air.
extra_html: Until the stump falls off, stick to sponge baths rather than submerging your baby. A small amount of dried blood or spotting as it separates is normal. The signs to watch for are infection: redness in the skin around the base, foul-smelling yellowish discharge, crying when you touch the cord, active bleeding, or fever — any of these is a reason to call your baby's doctor. This is general guidance; when in doubt about how the stump looks or smells, check with your pediatrician or health visitor.

related.title: Soothing a Fussy Newborn
related.hook: Newborns are wired to be calmed by sensations that echo the womb — holding, swaddling, gentle motion, white noise, and sucking. One rule overrides all: never, ever shake a baby.

flashcards.prompt: What's the best way to care for a newborn's umbilical cord stump?

choices.text: Keep it clean and dry and let it fall off on its own
Pull it off once it loosens

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP advises keeping the stump clean and dry as it shrivels and falls off naturally — no alcohol or special products are needed.

flashcards.prompt: What kind of bath should you give until the cord stump falls off?
flashcards.back_html: Sponge baths — keep the stump out of the water until it has fallen off on its own, usually by about three weeks.

flashcards.prompt: Which sign around the cord stump means you should call the doctor?

choices.text: Redness at the base, foul-smelling discharge, or active bleeding
A small amount of dried blood as it separates
The stump turning dark and shrivelled

flashcards.explanation_html: Redness, foul-smelling discharge, pain on touch, active bleeding, or fever can signal infection and warrant a call. A little dried blood and darkening are normal.
